About

I'm an SEO, AI search (AEO/GEO) and brand strategist. I help B2B brands get found on Google and named in the answers buyers now get from AI assistants.

My work starts with what a brand stands for, because search engines and AI assistants repeat what a brand says about itself. Then I build the pages, content and proof they can find, understand and quote, for brands selling in the US and India.

Selected work

AI search for a B2B video studio, US market

Got a small studio named inside Google's AI answers for buyer searches like "best b2b explainer video company in USA", where it is listed first. I wrote a content standard that AI can quote and gave each buyer niche its own page.

42.5K AI feature impressions4 buyer searches naming it2 US cities checked
Read the full case study

Situation

Motionvillee makes explainer videos for US B2B buyers, who now ask AI for a shortlist. It has about 3.4K linking domains, against about 15M for Clutch (SEOquake estimates). So I worked on making each page the clearest answer to one buyer question.

Problem

  • Rankings were personalised. Pages at #1 to #5 in Seattle showed at #6 to #28 from New York a week later.
  • The AI repeated the brand's own pages, mistakes included: West Chester, Ohio on 28 Sep, Seattle on 30 Sep.

What I did

  • A content standard AI can quote: a 40 to 60 word answer first, question headings, comparison tables, specific anchors, FAQ and author schema.
  • One service page per buyer niche: crypto and blockchain, cybersecurity, fintech.
  • A fixed framework for every "Motionvillee vs competitor" blog.
  • A "best explainer video companies in the USA" guide on Motionvillee's blog. It lists Motionvillee first and Google's AI quotes it. I disclose that openly.

Brand mapping and search for a new HR tech brand, India

Rebuilt the brand from real evidence: 8 live ads, 6 recorded sales calls and 7 buyer profiles. The ads sold six problems; customers confirmed two. The new positioning became a pitch deck, three landing pages, a client case study and the website.

≤32 days to an AI Overview citation#8 above Eightfold AI11 brand assets
Read the full case study

Situation

Staffjet.AI screens and interviews job candidates for Indian manufacturers. Less than six months old, its ads, website and sales team each told a different story.

Problem

  • The ads sold six problems. Customers confirmed two: reading resumes by hand takes days, and too many applications arrive at once.
  • Our headline claim, that buyers' HR systems never screen candidates, was wrong for 5 of the 25 platforms I checked.

What I did

  • Full brand mapping: positioning, messages for three buyer roles, competitor analysis, tone of voice, brand architecture and archetype.
  • Built the tone of voice from buyers' own words: "write like the buyer talks, not like a software category talks."
  • Removed unsourced claims. The new sales line asks what the buyer's system does today before comparing.
  • A sales pitch deck, three landing pages (BrandScript, Truth Funnel, pitch), a client case study and an internal team deck.
  • Helped plan and build staffjet.ai: sitemap, structure, copy, wireframes and SEO.
  • The blog's India buyer's guide ranks competitors fairly and puts Zoho Recruit first. Google's AI cites it for Zoho's pricing.

Still in progress: the broad term "ai recruiting software" sat at #40 on 30 Sep.

A buyer's guide that ranks competitors honestly is a page Google's AI will quote, even from a new brand. It also keeps the brand honest in front of buyers.

AI search for a new predictive maintenance brand

Google's AI uses an Insightvillee article to define "machine health signals" and names the brand, within 18 days of publishing. Another page ranks #3, right below IBM.

≤18 days to the AI definition#1 for two topics#3 below IBM
Read the full case study

Situation

Insightvillee sells AI predictive maintenance to plants. It is new, with about 300 linking domains against about 25M for IBM (SEOquake estimates). I helped plan and build insightvillee.com: sitemap, structure, copy, wireframes and SEO.

How the content works

  • Articles define the term first, then list what matters. The machine health signals post names all seven signals in its opening lines.
  • Separate pages per industry, such as chemical plants and automotive assembly.
  • The same AI-quotable content standard I use across brands.
SearchResult, 25 Sep
machine health signals#1 and the AI Overview definition
chemical plant maintenance with ai#1
what is an AI driven maintenance system#3 right below IBM

AI visibility came before traffic: 201 AI feature impressions and 44 clicks in three months. Clicks are the next thing to build.

Frameworks

PROOF Case StudyResult first, then the proof, so readers believe the win early.
Truth FunnelA landing page that earns agreement section by section before the ask.
Technical to Non-Technical PositioningEight steps to make a technical product matter to a non-technical buyer.
Brand MappingSix evidence-labelled questions that produce a brand's full documentation set.
Comparison BlogA fixed structure, AI prompt and checklist for "brand vs competitor" posts.
Engaging Simple WritingPlain English: short sentences, active voice, no jargon.
Blog Cluster BuilderA Claude skill that turns a topic list into an SEO cluster with internal links.

How I measure

Search Console first, because it is Google's own data and does not change with my browser. Screenshots show one day in one place, so each carries its date and, where shown, its location. Link counts are SEOquake estimates, used only to show the size of the gap.
